episodes.172349: A slow moving front caused showers and thunderstorms to develop. Deep moisture caused heavy rainfall, and with the slower movement of storms this led to instances of flooding and flash flooding.
episodes.173095: Strong upper-level ridging persisted and was the dominated weather feature for several days. Record breaking high temperatures, near single digit RH, and strong winds gusts have led to a Red Flag Warning throughout the 4 days. Numerous fires sparked as a result of incapsulated erratic gusty winds associated with isolated dry thunderstorms. The breakdown of the upper-level ridge, onset of strong winds aloft, and the isolated dry thunderstorms was the trifecta that led to an extreme critical fire weather event.
episodes.173212: Showers and storms developed in a moist airmass across the region. Some of these storms brought wind damage and small hail.
episodes.173230: A line of storms produced strong wind gusts as it passed through the Houston area during the afternoon.
episodes.173321: A cold front brought elevated thunderstorms with strong winds into southeast Oregon on the evening of September 7th, 2022.
episodes.173554: A few high based thunderstorms produced some severe wind gusts.
episodes.173787: A thunderstorm produced a funnel cloud near Shallotte.
episodes.174038: A boundary across Eastern North Carolina caused scattered showers and thunderstorms on the afternoon of September 7th.  While most of the thunderstorm were not strong, one isolated thunderstorm produced damage in northern Duplin County with strong winds.
episodes.174065: Tropical Storm Earl moved north of Puerto Rico early in the month. Although the storm never made landfall, it was responsible for shifting the local wind flow from the south. The islands were under this moist flow for around a week. Adding local effects to the mix, active afternoons were observed, with strong showers and thunderstorms. Several flood and mudslide reports were received.
episodes.174070: A surge of moisture moved over the islands during September 7th, increasing the frequency of showers. One of these showers generated a waterspout west of Culebra.
episodes.174154: A large upper trough extended from the Upper Midwest south into East Texas during the afternoon and evening of September 6th. At the surface, a moist and moderately unstable air mass was in place, with temperatures climbing into the lower 90s during the afternoon. With large scale forcing increasing ahead of the upper trough, isolated showers and thunderstorms developed over portions of Northwest Louisiana during the afternoon and evening, with one storm briefly becoming severe over Northern Bossier Parish, where damaging winds downed trees and power lines near Plain Dealing.
episodes.174186: An upper trough extended from the Great Lakes Region southwest into the Red River Valley during the morning hours of September 7th, which began to shift east across the Four State Region during the day. This trough reinforced a weak surface front south from Southeast Oklahoma and Southwest Arkansas into East Texas and North Louisiana throughout the day, with adequate moisture and instability present ahead of the front to help enhance scattered shower and thunderstorm development along and south of the front and ahead of the ejecting trough. Some of these storms became severe, with reports of damaging winds across portions of East Texas during the morning hours.
episodes.174188: An upper trough extended from the Great Lakes Region southwest into the Red River Valley during the morning hours of September 7th, which began to shift east across the Four State Region during the day. This trough reinforced a weak surface front south from Southeast Oklahoma and Southwest Arkansas into East Texas and North Louisiana throughout the day, with adequate moisture and instability present ahead of the front to help enhance scattered shower and thunderstorm development along and south of the front and ahead of the ejecting trough. Some of these storms became severe, with reports of damaging winds across portions of Southern Natchitoches Parish in Central Louisiana during the mid-afternoon hours.
episodes.174277: Scattered mainly diurnal thunderstorms developed along a slow moving low level boundary on September 6th and 7th.  A few of the storms focus for strong thunderstorms that produced isolated wind damage in Jefferson County and Sumter counties.
episodes.174500: A slow moving cold front draped across central Louisiana and Mississippi slowly but steadily moved southward through the local coastal waters. A warm and unstable environment was in place ahead of this front. The combination of lift from the front and buoyancy already in place provided a setup supportive for strong thunderstorm winds over various portions of the coastal waters as storms developed.
episodes.174501: A slow moving cold front draped across central Louisiana and Mississippi slowly but steadily moved southward through southeast Louisiana. A warm and unstable environment was in place ahead of this front. The combination of lift from the front and buoyancy already in place provided a setup supportive for a severe thunderstorm producing damaging winds near Baton Rouge.
episodes.174521: Thunderstorms produced high wind gusts along the coast.
episodes.174522: An upper level disturbance moved across the region producing scattered thunderstorms. A couple storms became severe.
